      How do collision models change a water-grown mixed aerosol?

      Studies / Worked examples / Coupled populations / Emissions and partitioning

      View code · Download Python script

      Matching saved results

      Execution: cuda:0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 · 2026-11-27 UTC · Script runtime: 3,040.93 s. Particula revision 20c50dad5. Executed source · Run metadata.

      How do collision models change a water-grown mixed aerosol?

      Section titled “How do collision models change a water-grown mixed aerosol?”

      A mixed aerosol can change size through water exchange and through collisions. How can we compare collision assumptions without confusing them with different starting populations? This example gives four scenarios copies of the same water-grown, particle-resolved aerosol, then compares their size spectra and one scenario’s particle composition.

      The organics–soot–water mixture is inspired by biomass-burning aerosol, but its properties and concentrations are illustrative. It is not a validated smoke plume or cloud parcel: temperature stays fixed, and there is no spatial flow, chemical aging, or wall removal. Use resolved coagulation and condensation first if the separate process contracts are unfamiliar.

      Python · section 1

      Build one mixed population and one finite vapor reservoir

      Section titled “Build one mixed population and one finite vapor reservoir”

      Sample 10,000 particles in 10⁻⁶ m³, giving 10¹⁰ m⁻³ initially. Independent organic and soot radius samples become masses in the same particle slots; these are not two externally mixed populations. Initial water mass equals organic plus soot mass, so particles already contain 50% water by mass.

      Densities are kg/m³ and molar masses kg/mol. Organic and soot κ values are 0.15 and 0.01; water occupies lane 2 and its own κ entry is unused. The default surface strategy supplies a water-like surface treatment, not a fitted composition-dependent smoke surface model.

      The variable named water_activity sets the initial gas saturation ratio to 1.02 at 298.15 K. It is not a prescribed liquid activity or humidity controller. Gas water can be depleted by condensation. The first histogram counts sampled radii per logarithmic bin; it has not yet been normalized by the represented volume.

      Python · section 2 
      Particle slots: 10000
Gas species: organics, soot, water

      Establish the shared water-grown starting state

      Section titled “Establish the shared water-grown starting state”

      Adaptive ROS3 integrates the same continuous condensation physics through a 0.01 s spin-up and a full 600 s preparation. The 601 stored states include both endpoints at one-second intervals after spin-up. The state labeled “Start” below includes this preparation; it is not the original dry population.

      The contour divides histogram counts by represented volume, giving number concentration per radius bin in m⁻³. It shows size redistribution, not dN/dr. The final species-inventory comparison includes both gas and weighted particle mass at rtol=10⁻¹² and atol=10⁻³⁰ kg. Conservation does not by itself establish timestep convergence, equilibration, or a physically calibrated activation threshold. A low final saturation ratio alone cannot diagnose numerical error.

      Change the collision model while retaining condensation

      Section titled “Change the collision model while retaining condensation”

      Each branch starts from a copy of the same shared state and advances a further 3600 s in 10,000 substeps (0.36 s each). The branches are condensation alone, Brownian plus condensation, combined Brownian/sedimentation plus condensation, and Saffman–Turner (1956) turbulent shear plus condensation.

      The shear branch replaces the earlier AO2008/DNS parameterization with the supported ST1956 kernel. It retains dissipation 1000 cm²/s³ (0.1 m²/s³) and fluid density 1.225 kg/m³; Reynolds lambda and relative velocity are not ST1956 inputs. It does not add separate Brownian or settling terms. Sedimentation causes collisions through differential settling, not removal. Its native mean-material-density convention is retained on the GPU.

      All four branches keep particle/gas state, physics and adaptive decisions on CUDA. The host schedules 0.36 s boundaries. Within each interval the collision sampler uses the live population to admit a duration, merges pairs, then recomputes the rate bound if time remains. Condensation follows once per outer interval. Only requested observations and diagnostics are downloaded. Direct collision pair evaluation replaces CPU bin interpolation. A persistent seeded GPU collision stream makes repeated GPU runs reproducible; it does not promise the same individual collisions as the former CPU sampler.

      The assertions test finite nonnegative masses and closed material inventories for each branch. Differences between one stochastic realization of each branch are not an ensemble estimate of a kernel’s effect.

      Convert counts into a comparable diameter spectrum

      Section titled “Convert counts into a comparable diameter spectrum”

      Exclude empty slots, double radius to obtain wet diameter, and bin particles between 0.01 and 100 µm. The spectrum uses the represented count per m³ and each bin’s measured log width. Convert the result to cm⁻³ per decade. This coordinate differs from the initial count histogram and the radius-bin contour, so compare integrated number with the appropriate measure rather than comparing raw vertical magnitudes.

      “Initial” means the original wet seeds; “Start” means the shared result of the condensation preparation. The four final curves add one hour to that state.

      Python · section 5

      Read the scenario overlay as a controlled model comparison

      Section titled “Read the scenario overlay as a controlled model comparison”

      The overlay uses the same binning and units for every scenario. Empty bins are hidden on logarithmic axes. Condensation moves sizes by exchanging vapor; coagulation reduces occupied particle count by merging material. A peak height alone does not measure total number or establish which process is dominant.

      The plot label “Brownian Only” identifies its collision kernel only; condensation also runs in that branch. Likewise, “with Sedimentation” combines Brownian and sedimentation kernels, while “with turbulent shear” uses the ST1956 kernel without the separate Brownian strategy.

      Python · section 6

      Keep the comparison’s evidence boundary in view

      Section titled “Keep the comparison’s evidence boundary in view”

      In this seeded run, Brownian coagulation plus settling needed two collision passes in 179 of the 10,000 intervals and merged 9,319 particle pairs. Brownian alone and turbulent shear each finished every interval in one pass, with 240 and 448 mergers respectively. The settling branch ended with 681 occupied slots. All four branches conserved the three species inventories. Comparison with the archived run

      All branches share their initial material inventory and retain the same condensation model. Their differing spectra therefore motivate a collision-model sensitivity study under these inputs. The plots and conservation checks do not establish a universal ordering of peak sizes or validate any kernel against a measured cloud. Repeated random seeds and temporal convergence are separate requirements for a quantitative comparison.

      Relate wet size to dry composition

      Section titled “Relate wet size to dry composition”

      The scatter plot compares the original wet seeds with the final shear-branch particles. Its horizontal coordinate is wet diameter, while its vertical coordinate is the dry organic fraction: organic mass divided by organic plus soot mass. Water is excluded from that denominator only in copied arrays; the simulation state remains unchanged.

      The comparison includes both the shared condensation preparation and the later shear-plus-condensation stage. It is not a before/after test of turbulence alone. A particle can shift horizontally by taking up water without changing its dry organic fraction.

      Python · section 7

      Avoid inferring a composition mechanism from size alone

      Section titled “Avoid inferring a composition mechanism from size alone”

      Merging particles can mix their dry fractions, while condensation changes wet size. A narrower band in the final scatter could reflect those effects and the sampled population. This plot alone does not demonstrate that turbulence selects organic-rich particles or leaves a distinct soot-rich mode. That claim would require a matched control and a quantified composition diagnostic.

      Turn the overlays into a research comparison

      Section titled “Turn the overlays into a research comparison”

      The example connects a common water-grown population to several collision assumptions and shows why both size and composition diagnostics are useful. A conserved material inventory supports interpretation of transfers, but does not choose the most accurate cloud model.

      For a next study, compare every branch with the same post-preparation state, repeat independent seeds, and report total number, wet-size quantiles, and dry organic-fraction distributions. Vary turbulent dissipation while holding other inputs fixed, then test timestep and sampling convergence. Measured size and composition data would be needed to attribute a real smoke–cloud response to one collision mechanism.
